paragraphs: Vector Symbolic Architectures provide a way to perform symbolic operations using real-valued vectors. Their central operation is binding: combining two vectors into another vector of the same dimensionality. This lets a system represent combinations of information without making the representation longer every time something is added. The paper places this approach within the broader effort to connect neural computation with symbolic manipulation.

The algebraic properties of binding matter because they determine which manipulations the representation supports. The abstract describes commutativity, associativity, and an inverse operation, which provide structure for combining and recovering information. However, many existing architectures originated in systems whose operations were designed by hand, before automatic differentiation became a routine part of neural-network development.

The paper introduces Hadamard-derived linear Binding, or HLB, to address that design context. Its stated goals combine computational efficiency, effectiveness on established vector-symbolic tasks, and suitability for differentiable systems. The contribution is a binding architecture designed with both symbolic operations and modern neural learning in mind.
neurips-2024-a-walsh-hadamard-derived-li.tldr: HLB introduces a vector-binding architecture designed for efficient symbolic operations and use in differentiable learning systems.

paragraphs: Optimizing a diffusion model's starting latent variables or parameters requires understanding how changes affect its final output. That becomes difficult when generation involves solving a differential equation through many intermediate states. Ordinary backpropagation stores those states, creating substantial memory demands. Stochastic diffusion adds another complication because the generation process injects noise along the way.

AdjointDEIS approaches gradient computation through continuous adjoint equations, which describe how output sensitivity propagates through the continuous generation process. The paper develops numerical solvers specifically for these equations rather than treating them as arbitrary differential equations. It uses exponential integrators and the structure of diffusion processes to simplify the computation, and provides guarantees for the solvers' convergence order.

A central result is that the continuous adjoint equations associated with diffusion stochastic differential equations simplify to an ordinary differential equation. This makes the sensitivity problem more tractable despite the noise in generation. The authors demonstrate the method in guided generation through an adversarial face-morphing application, supporting its usefulness for optimizing outputs against a differentiable objective.
neurips-2024-adjointdeis-efficient-gradi.tldr: AdjointDEIS develops diffusion-specific differential-equation solvers for computing gradients, with convergence guarantees and a guided-generation demonstration.

paragraphs: Combining code-training datasets can increase variety, but it also brings together incompatible styles and uneven quality. AlchemistCoder addresses this tension when fine-tuning pretrained code language models. The motivation is that relying on a single data source may leave useful capabilities underdeveloped, while simply pooling sources does not resolve conflicts between their instructions and responses.

The method introduces AlchemistPrompts, prompts tailored to particular data through hindsight relabeling. These prompts help reconcile the differences among sources and their instruction-response pairs. The authors also turn parts of the data-construction process into training material. Instruction evolution, data filtering, and code review become code-comprehension tasks, giving the model additional ways to learn from how examples are constructed and assessed.

The resulting model family is evaluated for code generation and generalization. In the reported experiments, the 6.7-billion- and 7-billion-parameter models lead their same-size comparisons and compete with, or sometimes exceed, larger models. These findings support the value of organizing heterogeneous training data and teaching comprehension alongside generation, rather than treating dataset diversity alone as sufficient.
neurips-2024-alchemistcoder-harmonizing-.tldr: AlchemistCoder combines hindsight-based prompts and code-comprehension tasks to improve fine-tuning on heterogeneous code datasets.

paragraphs: Agents helping different people cannot assume that they all possess the same information. Each may initially have access only to its own user's messages and context, even when completing a task requires knowledge held by someone else. This paper studies that information asymmetry as a central obstacle to collaboration among language-model agents.

The proposed iAgents system mirrors the human social network with a network of agents. Agents proactively exchange information needed for the shared task. A reasoning mechanism called InfoNav directs communication toward useful exchanges, while a mixed-memory system organizes human information so agents can retrieve and communicate relevant material. Together, these components address both finding missing information and obtaining it from other participants.

The authors also introduce InformativeBench to evaluate task solving under unequal information access. Their experiments demonstrate collaboration in a network containing 140 people and 588 relationships, with autonomous conversations exceeding 30 turns and retrieval across nearly 70,000 messages. Tasks are completed within three minutes in the reported setting, illustrating the system's ability to coordinate communication and retrieval at that scale.
neurips-2024-autonomous-agents-for-colla.tldr: iAgents coordinates information exchange among personal agents so they can collaborate when each starts with different knowledge.

paragraphs: In-context learning is usually associated with causal language models, which generate text by predicting what comes next. This paper asks whether masked language models can also exhibit that ability. The distinction matters because an architecture's usual training objective may obscure capabilities that become accessible through a different way of using it at inference time.

The authors demonstrate generative in-context learning with an existing DeBERTa model using a simple inference technique. The approach requires neither additional training nor architectural changes. The contribution therefore concerns how an already trained masked model is used: it shows that generative task performance can be elicited without first rebuilding the model as a causal language model.

The evaluation finds different strengths across task categories, with masked and causal models each clearly outperforming the other in different areas. This supports a broader view of in-context learning across architectures, rather than establishing one architecture as uniformly superior. The authors suggest that hybrid approaches could combine these complementary strengths; the abstract presents that as a promising direction, rather than an evaluated hybrid system.
neurips-2024-berts-are-generative-in-con.tldr: A simple inference technique enables DeBERTa to perform generative in-context learning without retraining, revealing strengths complementary to causal models.

paragraphs: Tracking a moving object becomes especially difficult when its appearance in a video breaks expected continuity across space or time. A tracker then needs effective visual search, rather than only precise localization near the last known position. This paper studies those discontinuities through a human-inspired account of central and peripheral vision.

The proposed CPDTrack gives the two forms of vision complementary roles. Its central component uses continuity across video frames to introduce prior information and improve localization precision. Its peripheral component maintains broader awareness and detects object movement. The approach connects detailed local tracking with a wider search process, addressing situations where following the immediate neighborhood alone is insufficient.

The authors also create STDChallenge, a benchmark specifically for assessing visual search across these discontinuities, and include human participants to establish a behavioral baseline. Their experiments report state-of-the-art performance on the challenge, smaller behavioral differences from humans, and strong generalization across other difficult benchmarks. The contribution therefore includes both a tracker and an evaluation setting that examines how tracking behavior compares with human search.
neurips-2024-beyond-accuracy-tracking-mo.tldr: CPDTrack combines central and peripheral visual processing to improve tracking through discontinuities and narrow measured behavioral differences from humans.

paragraphs: Best-of-n sampling aligns language-model outputs by generating several candidates, ranking them, and returning the best. This paper examines how that selection procedure relates to reinforcement learning from human feedback. It also asks whether a model can learn the resulting output distribution so that generating multiple candidates is no longer required at every inference.

The theoretical result connects best-of-n sampling to an RLHF policy under a particular monotone transformation of the reward function. With that transformation, the distribution achieves an optimal trade-off between beating the base model in preference comparisons and remaining close to its distribution, measured by KL distance. This is a specific Pareto-optimality result for win rate and distributional change, rather than a claim of optimality for every alignment objective.

The authors derive BoNBoN Alignment to fine-tune a model toward the best-of-n distribution. This transfers the benefit of selection into the model's sampling behavior. Experiments report high win rates with minimal effects on aspects of generation outside the alignment target, supporting the practical value of preserving base-model behavior while improving preferred responses.
neurips-2024-bonbon-alignment-for-large-.tldr: BoNBoN trains models to imitate best-of-n sampling, supported by a theoretical connection to an optimal win-rate-versus-KL alignment trade-off.

paragraphs: Learning visual features without labels requires a training objective that preserves useful differences between images. The paper examines I-JEPA, which learns through masked-image representation prediction. It identifies two problems: the exponential moving average mechanism does not prevent complete representation collapse, and the prediction objective does not adequately learn the mean of patch representations.

C-JEPA combines I-JEPA with Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization, or VICReg. The added regularization addresses several aspects of representation structure together. Variance and covariance information help prevent the representations from collapsing, while invariance aligns the means of different augmented views. The goal is to retain meaningful variability while making representations consistent across related versions of an image.

The authors support the framework with theoretical and empirical evaluations, reporting improved training stability and representation quality. After pretraining on ImageNet-1K, C-JEPA shows faster and improved convergence in linear probing and fine-tuning evaluations. These findings suggest that explicitly controlling representation statistics can strengthen the predictive learning approach, addressing weaknesses that the existing averaging and prediction mechanisms do not adequately resolve.
neurips-2024-connecting-joint-embedding-.tldr: C-JEPA adds variance, invariance, and covariance regularization to I-JEPA to improve representation stability and quality.

paragraphs: Credit attribution asks which training contributions meaningfully influence an algorithm's output. This paper approaches that question through stability: if changing a data point has no significant effect, its influence is controlled. The authors introduce relaxations of differential privacy that allow a designated set of k data points to receive weaker stability protection.

Those designated points may be used in a way that substantially affects the output, with their owners' permission and potentially compensation. The remaining points retain guarantees against significant influence. This separates the data allowed to shape an output strongly from data whose individual effect must remain limited, giving the attribution problem a formal learning-theoretic structure.

The framework encompasses several existing settings. Setting k to zero recovers differential privacy; fixing the designated points in advance connects to private learning with public data; selecting them adaptively connects to stable sample compression. The paper characterizes learnability under these notions within the PAC learning framework. Its main contribution is therefore a unified account of what algorithms can learn while controlling which data points may exert substantial influence.
neurips-2024-credit-attribution-and-stab.tldr: The paper formalizes credit attribution through stability guarantees that permit substantial influence from a designated, authorized subset of training data.

paragraphs: A small preview of a dataset may need to support a much larger purchasing decision. The buyer wants to know whether the vendor's underlying data source will be useful, not merely what the preview itself is worth. This paper reframes data valuation around the distributions that generate datasets, using observed samples to compare those distributions.

The proposed method uses maximum mean discrepancy, or MMD, as the basis of its valuation. Its theoretical treatment assumes a Huber characterization of differences between vendors' data. Under that model of heterogeneity, the method supports principled and actionable comparison policies. This assumption is part of the foundation for the theory, rather than an unrestricted claim about every possible collection of data sources.

The experiments evaluate whether useful distributions can be identified efficiently from samples. Across real-world datasets, including intrusion and credit-card-fraud detection, and across classification and regression applications, the method performs effectively against existing baselines. The reported sample efficiency matters for settings where only limited previews are available before committing to acquiring more data.
neurips-2024-data-distribution-valuation.tldr: The paper uses MMD to compare the value of data-generating distributions from samples under a specified model of vendor heterogeneity.

paragraphs: This paper develops an algorithm for testing whether two continuous distributions are equivalent while protecting individual data points through differential privacy. It builds on a method that repeatedly partitions the real line using observed data. When distributions differ sufficiently in the specified A_k norm, a suitable partition exposes a detectable difference between the resulting discrete distributions.

Privatizing that procedure is difficult because changing one observation can substantially shift a partition boundary in value. The authors instead use the observation's position in sorted order, which changes by only one between neighboring datasets. A new mechanism adds Bernoulli randomness when choosing partition points, allowing only a few buckets to be affected under an appropriate coupling.

The private procedure also avoids resampling, so the original correctness argument must be rebuilt around the already sorted data. The authors handle this using subsets whose sizes are drawn from a Poisson distribution within each bin. They further carry the method to other distribution families through reductions to continuous distributions, extending the reach of the private testing construction.
neurips-2024-differentially-private-equi.tldr: The paper introduces a differentially private test for continuous-distribution equivalence using randomized partitions based on sorted data positions.

paragraphs: Graph diffusion computations underpin tools such as Personalized PageRank, Katz centrality, and the heat kernel. Standard iterative methods revisit the entire graph at each step, which becomes expensive on large graphs. Existing local methods reduce that work, but often rely on sequential heuristics tailored to one particular kind of diffusion.

The paper develops a more general framework around the local concentration of diffusion vectors, measured through the participation ratio. A local diffusion process makes it possible to approximate these vectors without treating every part of the graph equally. The framework exposes shortcomings of existing local solvers and turns standard iterative methods into local algorithms with provably sublinear running time.

The resulting solvers are also highly parallelizable, making them suitable for GPUs. Experiments report speed improvements of up to a hundred-fold and demonstrate use on large dynamic graphs. These are results for approximate diffusion computation, where locality can reduce the work needed. The authors additionally suggest that the framework could support more efficient local message passing in graph neural networks.
neurips-2024-faster-local-solvers-for-gr.tldr: A general local-diffusion framework yields parallelizable approximate graph solvers with sublinear-time guarantees and reported speedups of up to a hundred-fold.

paragraphs: Surface parameterization connects a three-dimensional surface to a two-dimensional coordinate domain. Traditional methods often expect carefully constructed meshes and require manual cuts or segmentation when topology becomes complicated. Flatten Anything Model, or FAM, aims to automate this process while accepting less structured geometric data.

FAM learns mappings between points on a 3D surface and adaptively changing 2D UV coordinates. Its component networks have geometric roles corresponding to cutting, deforming UV coordinates, unwrapping, and wrapping. These components form a bidirectional cycle, linking the flattened representation back to the original surface. The learning process discovers cutting seams and boundaries instead of requiring a person to specify them beforehand.

The model operates directly on discrete surface points without needing connectivity information. This reduces its dependence on mesh quality and permits use with unstructured point clouds. The authors report extensive experiments supporting applicability to complex topologies and advantages over previous methods. The central contribution is a learned parameterization process that combines automatic boundary selection with a less restrictive input representation.
neurips-2024-flatten-anything-unsupervis.tldr: FAM learns to flatten 3D surfaces automatically from discrete points, discovering seams and UV boundaries without requiring mesh connectivity.

paragraphs: Multiobjective optimization produces trade-offs rather than a single solution that is best on every objective. A useful summary therefore needs several Pareto-optimal solutions distributed across the available trade-offs. This paper asks how to choose K such solutions so they represent the whole Pareto front instead of concentrating in a small region.

The authors introduce fill distance as a measure of representativeness. It captures the largest gap between the front and its nearest selected design point, making uncovered regions central to evaluation. Directly minimizing this quantity creates a difficult nested optimization problem. The proposed alternative is a max-packing design, which is easier to optimize and encourages the selected solutions to spread apart.

The surrogate comes with a guarantee: its fill distance is at most four times the minimum achievable value, and the design is rate-optimal. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks report efficient production of representative, high-quality solutions and improvements over baselines. The result connects a tractable selection strategy to a quantitative coverage guarantee, rather than relying only on visual impressions of uniformity.
neurips-2024-gliding-over-the-pareto-fro.tldr: A max-packing surrogate selects representative Pareto-optimal solutions with fill distance guaranteed to be within four times the optimum.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a three-dimensional hand from one color image requires inferring joints and shape despite complex articulation, hidden fingers, and nearby objects. Hamba targets the relationships between joints, which the authors identify as insufficiently modeled by existing attention-based approaches. Its design combines graph learning with Mamba's state-space modeling.

The central change is to guide Mamba's scanning process with the hand's graph structure and scan in both directions. A Graph-guided State Space block learns joint relationships and spatial sequences using a compact set of tokens. The reported token count is 88.5% lower than that of attention-based methods. A separate fusion module combines these structured features with global features so reconstruction can use both local joint information and broader image context.

Across benchmarks and in-the-wild tests, the authors report substantial improvements over existing leading methods. On FreiHAND, Hamba achieves 5.3 mm PA-MPVPE and an F@15mm score of 0.992. It also held first place on two reconstruction competition leaderboards at acceptance. These findings support the effectiveness of the graph-guided representation in the evaluated reconstruction settings.
neurips-2024-hamba-single-view-3d-hand-r.tldr: Hamba uses graph-guided bidirectional Mamba scanning to model hand joints compactly and improve single-image 3D hand reconstruction.

paragraphs: A mobile assistant must keep track of what it has already accomplished and which screen content remains relevant. Long histories mixing screenshots and text make both tasks difficult for a single multimodal agent. Mobile-Agent-v2 addresses this navigation problem by distributing responsibility among planning, decision, and reflection agents.

The planning agent converts the operation history and screen summaries into a concise, text-only account of task progress. The decision agent uses that account to choose subsequent actions, reducing the amount of mixed visual and textual history it must process. A memory unit retains relevant content and is updated as the task advances, helping preserve information that would otherwise be lost during summarization.

The reflection agent examines the outcome of each operation and responds to mistakes. Together, these components separate progress tracking, action selection, and error handling while maintaining shared task context. Experiments report more than a 30% improvement in task completion over the single-agent Mobile-Agent architecture. This supports the value of coordinated roles and explicit memory for the evaluated mobile-operation tasks.
neurips-2024-mobile-agent-v2-mobile-devi.tldr: Mobile-Agent-v2 coordinates planning, decision, and reflection agents to improve task tracking, relevant-content memory, and mobile-operation completion.

paragraphs: Multi-label learning allows several labels to apply to the same example. Training usually minimizes a surrogate loss that is easier to optimize than the actual evaluation loss. This paper studies how well surrogate optimization translates into good predictions within a hypothesis class, using H-consistency bounds to make that connection quantitative.

For Hamming loss, the authors show that binary relevance with smooth losses such as logistic loss has an unfavorable dependence on the number of labels in these bounds. It also ignores label correlations. Their proposed multi-label logistic loss accounts for those correlations and obtains label-independent H-consistency bounds, directly addressing both weaknesses of the simpler formulation.

The analysis then expands to multi-label comp-sum losses and constrained losses, with H-consistency and resulting Bayes-consistency guarantees across general multi-label losses. The covered evaluation losses include common choices and a linear-fractional family based on the confusion matrix. Efficient gradient-computation algorithms accompany the logistic formulation. The contribution combines broader theoretical guarantees with algorithms for optimizing the proposed loss.
neurips-2024-multi-label-learning-with-s.tldr: The paper develops correlation-aware multi-label surrogate losses with stronger consistency guarantees and efficient gradient computation.

paragraphs: Omnigrasp studies how a simulated humanoid can grasp an object and carry it along a desired trajectory. This requires coordinating a full body with dexterous hands over an extended movement. Earlier approaches often simplified the problem to a detached hand performing a vertical lift or following a short path, limiting their usefulness for broader animation and simulation tasks.

The method builds on a humanoid motion representation that supplies human-like motor skills and substantially accelerates training. With this representation, the controller learns to pick up more than 1,200 objects and follow randomly generated trajectories. The authors report that simple reward, state, and object representations are sufficient for favorable scaling across diverse objects and paths.

Training does not require paired examples of full-body motion and object trajectories. At test time, the controller needs the object's mesh and the desired trajectory for grasping and transport. Reported results show state-of-the-art success rates for trajectory following and generalization to unseen objects, supporting the approach's ability to extend manipulation beyond narrowly specified lifts.
neurips-2024-omnigrasp-grasping-diverse-.tldr: Omnigrasp uses a humanoid motion representation to train simulated full-body controllers that grasp diverse objects and transport them along desired trajectories.

paragraphs: Selective classifiers can decline to make predictions when confidence is low. Evaluating them only at a fixed rejection threshold gives a narrow view of performance, because changing that threshold changes which predictions are accepted. This paper seeks a general evaluation measure spanning thresholds, analogous in purpose to AUROC for ordinary classification.

The authors define five requirements covering alignment with the task, interpretability, and flexibility, and show that existing approaches do not satisfy them all. They propose the Area under the Generalized Risk Coverage curve, or AUGRC. The metric meets the stated requirements and can be interpreted directly as the average risk of failures that remain undetected rather than being rejected.

The empirical study covers six datasets and thirteen confidence-scoring functions. Using AUGRC substantially changes the resulting rankings on five datasets, showing that the evaluation choice can materially affect conclusions about which approaches perform best. The contribution is a way to assess selective prediction across operating thresholds while preserving an interpretation tied to the errors the system allows through.
neurips-2024-overcoming-common-flaws-in-.tldr: AUGRC evaluates selective classifiers across rejection thresholds and interprets performance as average undetected-failure risk.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning controllers improve through interaction, but exploratory actions can be unpredictable. That creates a problem in critical control settings where safety must hold during learning itself. RL with Adaptive Regularization, or RL-AR, combines a learned policy with a policy regularizer in which safety constraints are explicitly encoded.

A focus module determines how much the combined controller should rely on each policy at the current state. In states that have received less exploration, it places more weight on the safe regularizer. In well-exploited states, it allows the learned policy to converge without bias from that regularization. The balance therefore changes with the state rather than imposing the same restriction everywhere.

The authors demonstrate the approach across a series of critical control applications. They report safety throughout training together with returns competitive with model-free reinforcement learning that disregards safety. These findings support adaptive policy combination as a way to retain protective behavior during exploration while allowing useful learned behavior to emerge where the controller has accumulated more experience.
neurips-2024-reinforcement-learning-with.tldr: RL-AR adaptively combines a learned controller with an explicitly constrained safe policy, reporting safe training and competitive returns.

paragraphs: Diffusion models for time-series forecasting can suffer from unstable performance when training data are insufficient and generation lacks useful guidance. Retrieval-Augmented Time series Diffusion, or RATD, addresses these problems by bringing relevant examples from a database into the forecasting process. The retrieved series serve as references for generation.

The framework first uses embeddings to identify database time series relevant to the historical series being forecast. A reference-guided diffusion model then uses those examples during denoising. This connects retrieval with sampling: stored examples actively inform the production of a forecast, increasing the use made of meaningful data already present in the database.

The authors evaluate the approach through experiments and visualizations on multiple datasets, reporting particular effectiveness on complicated prediction tasks. The findings support the idea that relevant references can supply guidance missing from existing diffusion forecasters. The contribution lies in the combination of an embedding-based search stage and a denoising process designed to use its results, rather than treating retrieval as a separate preprocessing output.
neurips-2024-retrieval-augmented-diffusi.tldr: RATD retrieves relevant historical time series and uses them to guide diffusion-based forecasts, with reported benefits on complex prediction tasks.

paragraphs: Social relation reasoning assigns categories such as friends, spouses, or colleagues to people depicted in images. SocialGPT divides this task into visual perception and language-based reasoning. A vision foundation model first describes the image as a social story, and a language model then uses that text to infer the relationship.

The framework includes design principles for adapting the visual and language components separately and connecting their outputs. Without additional model training, it achieves competitive zero-shot results on two databases. The language model also produces verbal explanations of its decisions, making the reasoning output accessible as text alongside the predicted relationship category.

Designing the reasoning prompt manually is laborious, and converting visual classification into text generation introduces a long-prompt optimization problem. The authors address it with Greedy Segment Prompt Optimization, which uses gradient information to guide a greedy search over prompt segments. Experiments show significant performance improvements from this procedure and generalization across image styles. The paper thus combines a modular recognition system with a method for improving the prompts that coordinate its reasoning.
neurips-2024-socialgpt-prompting-llms-fo.tldr: SocialGPT converts images into textual social stories for relationship reasoning and improves performance through segment-level prompt optimization.

paragraphs: Recovering a correct ranking from a crowd becomes difficult when most voters are misinformed. Surprisingly popular voting uses both voters' answers and their predictions about other voters to help recover information held by a knowledgeable minority. However, requesting full rankings and probability distributions becomes burdensome when there are many alternatives.

The paper introduces Aggregated-SP and Partial-SP to reduce that reporting burden. Voters provide an answer and a prediction for a much smaller subset of alternatives, using a top choice, partial ranking, or approval set. These variants adapt the surprisingly popular approach to partial preferences, making its information requirements more manageable as the number of alternatives grows.

A large MTurk experiment finds that both methods outperform conventional aggregation approaches on ranking recovery, measured by Kendall-Tau distance and Spearman's rho. The authors also show that a concentric mixture of Mallows models can reproduce observed voting behavior, including minority expertise and the surprisingly popular phenomenon. Sample-complexity bounds provide theoretical support for using partial rankings in these methods.
neurips-2024-the-surprising-effectivenes.tldr: Two surprisingly popular voting variants use partial preferences to reduce reporting costs while improving ranking recovery in a crowdsourcing experiment.

paragraphs: Developing adaptive reinforcement-learning agents requires environments that can vary in layout and task rules. Building those environments can itself consume substantial research effort. United Unity Universe, or U3, is an open-source toolkit intended to make environment creation and experimentation easier by combining XLand's flexibility with Unity's rapid-prototyping capabilities.

The toolkit includes an implementation of XLand 2.0 and an interface for modifying procedurally generated terrains and rules. It also supplies a curated set of terrains and rule sets, together with reinforcement-learning baseline implementations. These components give researchers starting environments and reference agents so they can move more directly into experiments with new agent architectures.

The authors present U3 as a high-level language for constructing diverse, continually variable three-dimensional environments within one framework. Its contribution is research infrastructure: it makes variation in environments and tasks easier to express and reuse. The intended benefit is faster experimentation on adaptive and generalizable learning systems, with the toolkit supporting the creation of the settings in which those capabilities can be studied.
neurips-2024-using-unity-to-help-solve-r.tldr: U3 combines XLand 2.0 and Unity into an open-source toolkit for rapidly building varied 3D reinforcement-learning environments.

paragraphs: Wearable heart-rate estimates commonly rely on photoplethysmography, or PPG, but movement, sensor placement, light, and temperature can disrupt the signal. WildPPG examines performance during varied everyday activities outside controlled recording conditions. The authors find that leading estimation methods struggle on this data, plausibly because existing training datasets emphasize more controlled situations.

The dataset follows 16 participants during a day-long trip from Zurich to Jungfraujoch. It contains 13.5-hour recordings per participant, totaling 216 hours, with four wearable sensors positioned at different body locations. Measurements include acceleration, temperature, and altitude, alongside synchronized Lead I electrocardiography that supplies reference heart rates. Activities include walking, hiking, stairs, meals, rest, and several forms of transport.

These continuous recordings capture changing behavior and environments, including altitudes reaching 3,571 meters, within the same trip. The dataset and benchmark results support evaluation under those varied conditions. The paper also introduces a heart-rate estimation method that performs more robustly than existing baselines in the studied real-world scenarios, pairing a challenging evaluation resource with an improved approach.
neurips-2024-wildppg-a-real-world-ppg-da.tldr: WildPPG provides long, multimodal wearable recordings from varied everyday activities and a method that improves heart-rate estimation robustness on them.
